## Hive 0.8.0 — usage events and your installation ID
Hive now sends small usage events with a random installation ID, and Settings shows that ID.
### New
- **Usage events.** Hive sends one small event when it is installed, when it is updated and at most once a day when it is opened. It carries only a random installation ID, the app name, the type of event, the Hive version and build, the macOS version, the type of Mac (architecture) and a timestamp. It never carries your name, the name of your computer, folders, organization or project names, terminal content, environment variables or language. The ID is random and does not identify you by itself. Like any server, the registry receives your IP address; the privacy policy says it is kept only in the server logs, for 30 days, and not with the events. There is no switch to turn the events off. The events are sent in the background and never delay Hive: if the network is off or the server refuses them, Hive ignores it and tries again the next time it opens. - **Installation ID.** Settings › General shows the random identifier of this installation, with a Copy button that confirms with "Copied". It is the same identifier sent with the usage events, so you can quote it if you ask for those events to be deleted. Settings shows "Not generated yet" until Hive has opened once with this version. - **Privacy policy and terms of use.** Settings › General has buttons that open both pages in your browser, in the language of the app.
### Fixed
- The organization profile sheet no longer grows past the Hive window: its content scrolls and Cancel and Save stay visible.
---
*Hive is made by Zeep Labs.*

## Hive 0.7.0 — agents that test your Mac apps, and a document viewer
Claude Code agents opened by Hive can now open, read and control Mac apps to test them, with your approval for each session. And the files an agent mentions in the terminal now open inside Hive.
### New
- **Computer use (beta, off by default).** Turn on "Computer use by agents" in an organization's profile and Claude Code agents in sessions opened after that can list apps and windows, read a window, click, type, scroll, press keys and check what is on screen. It works in the background when the app allows it, and every action reports whether its effect was confirmed. - **Approval per session.** The first time an agent needs the computer, Hive asks you. You choose whether it may use only the app it asked for or any app, and whether it may use the mouse and keyboard in the foreground (off by default). The approval lasts until the session ends. The session tab shows when an agent can use the computer and when it is acting, and Stop takes the approval back at once. - **Tests tab.** When an agent runs a test, each step is recorded with a small screenshot, and the right panel's new Tests tab shows the runs of the visible project with their steps and results. - **Permissions guide.** Settings shows which macOS permissions computer use needs and opens the right place in System Settings. - **Document viewer.** Cmd-click on a file path in the terminal opens the file in a tab of the project. Markdown is shown formatted (headings, lists, task lists, tables, code blocks, quotes, links), JSON and YAML get colors, and other text files are shown as plain text. The tab updates when the agent rewrites the file and shows "removed" if it disappears. Cmd-F searches the document. It is read-only, never loads images or anything from the internet, and never runs a file: only plain text goes to the default app, and everything else goes to your code editor or the Finder. - **Code editor.** In Settings › General you can choose VS Code, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, Xcode or Nova. Cmd-click on a code file then opens it in that editor, at the cited line when the editor supports it, and the project's context menu gets "Open in <editor>". With no editor chosen, code opens as text in a Hive tab. Hive never hands code to the default app of its extension.
### Improved
- The scroll indicator of the right panel is thinner and follows the light and dark themes, and the sidebar no longer shows one.
### Fixed
- The terminal could stay smaller or larger than its panel after the screen was locked or the window moved to another monitor. It now fits the panel again by itself. - Cmd-click on a path at the end of a sentence ("see /repo/spec.md.") failed with "Link blocked" because the final period was taken as part of the path. A path that does not exist now shows a short notice instead of that alert.
### Security
- Hive itself never gets Accessibility or Screen Recording. Those permissions belong to a separate helper app inside Hive, "Hive Computer Use", which only answers Hive. Programs your agents run in the terminal do not inherit them. - The Hive that runs the session, System Settings, Keychain Access, password managers, terminals and script runners (Terminal, iTerm2, Script Editor, Automator, Shortcuts and similar), the Apple menu and system shortcuts (quit, log out, lock the screen, force quit) are always blocked, whatever you approve. - The agent sees a screenshot only when it asks for one, menus stay collapsed until it opens one, and passwords in secure fields are never read back. What the agent reads from the screen goes to its model provider, and the approval dialog says so. - The document viewer opens any file you Cmd-click, but only shows it on your screen: no network request, no execution, files above 5 MB or that are not text are refused. - Test screenshots stay on this Mac, in Hive's data folder. They are deleted after 14 days or when they pass 100 MB, and together with their project or organization.
### Known limits
- Tested with native Mac apps and Google Chrome. Safari pages may not show up for the agent; use Chrome for web tests. - In Chrome, clicking web content needs the foreground option. - Keys sent in the background did not reach the system Open and Save panel of TextEdit in our test; use the foreground option for those panels. - Only Claude Code agents opened by Hive can use the computer. - Document tabs do not come back after you restart Hive. Opening a file at a line (`file:12`) works only in editors that support it (VS Code and Cursor). - Markdown shows tables and code blocks with square corners, and a second paragraph inside a list item is joined to the item. - Not yet verified: macOS 14 and 15, Electron apps, the iOS Simulator and VoiceOver on the new screens.
---
*Hive is made by Zeep Labs.*

## Hive 0.6.0 — delegate to projects, and what's new
Agents can now hand work to a whole project, not only to a session that is already open, and Hive tells you what changed after each update.
### New
- **Automatic delegation (experimental, off by default).** In an organization's profile you can turn on "Approve and open sessions automatically". With it on, a Claude Code agent can list the organization's projects and delegate a task or mention to a project. Hive approves it on its own and, if the project has no Claude session, opens one in a separate worktree. Turning it on asks you to confirm the risk, and you can turn it off at any time from the right panel. - **Delegated sessions are marked.** Sessions that Hive opened for a delegation show a mark in the tab and in the tree, with the project they came from. - **"Needs a session" notification.** If Hive could not open a session for a delegated task, it tells you which project is waiting. A waiting task is dropped after 10 minutes. - **What's new.** The first time you open a new version, Hive shows its highlights. You can open it again from Help › What's New in Hive. - **Clickable links in the terminal.** Links are underlined when you hover them. Hold ⌘ and click to open one. - **Right panel redrawn.** Requests and PRs follow the rest of the app, and the PRs tab shows a loading state while it fetches.
### Improved
- The "default account" notice on the PRs tab is now a card. - The requests panel shows when automatic approval is on, with a shortcut to turn it off.
### Fixed
- The Agent Board could hang the app when macOS was set to always show scroll bars.
### Security
- Automatic mode never turns on from an agent or from a command line: only from the organization's profile, after you confirm. - Hive never accepts a folder trust prompt for you. A session opened by delegation waits until you answer it in the terminal. - Automatic delegation only works inside one organization, and a project from another organization looks the same as one that does not exist.
### Known limits
- When several sessions are opened by delegation at the same time, the first message to a new session may not be confirmed within 10 seconds, and Hive does not resend it. Ask the sending agent again if that happens. - Not yet verified: organizations with their own Claude config folder (the trust prompt may appear more often), macOS 14 and 15, and VoiceOver on the new screens. - A program running as you on this Mac can change Hive's local settings file, including this option. Turn it on only where you trust the agents you run.
---
*Hive is made by Zeep Labs.*
